text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Money loaned to the impecunious the Vietnam Bank for the Poor since the beginning of this year was 1.80 trillion dong ($155 million) following advances to an additional 100,000 needy households throughout the country.
-- Deputy Prime Minister Tran Duc Luong has been included on the list of foreigners to be awarded the Russian Federation's Friendship Order.

-- A visit to Saigon Port on Tuesday by the British naval class 22 frigate HMS Beaver, which coincided with British Week in the southern city, is a symbolic and visible demonstration of the close and growing relationship between Britain and Vietnam.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has given a green light to exports of wooden products included in last year's quota, but such exports must be completed by September 30 at the latest.

-- Deputy Prime Minister Tran Duc Luong said construction of a road linking Thailand's eastern region to Vietnam's central coast through Laos would serve the interests of all people in the sub-Mekong region.
-- Appeals by 19 of the 22 defendants convicted in the Vu Xuan Truong heroin-trafficking case will be heard from June 24 to June 30.
